reasons.A: Short plain declaratives with occasional fragments, flat understated stance, no rhetorical questions, ends on a quiet concrete image, which is closest to the passage's movement and tone.
reasons.C: Sentence length and plainness are close, but the rhetorical 'So why keep it up?' and neat aphorisms ('The paper does not miss much, but I had') are more crafted and reflective than the author.
reasons.D: Piles on clipped fragments ('By hand. With newspaper.', 'Round and round.') more thickly than the passage, adds second-person 'you' and a moralising close; reads as caricature.
reasons.B: Long multi-clause sentences, a semicolon, explanatory and hedged register ('roughly', 'partly'), a rhetorical question and essayistic wrap-up; furthest from the author's terse plain voice.
